questions.question: Why can't you use the same scoring strategy for all document types in a multimodal RAG system?
choices: It's technically impossible to score everything the same way
Images don't have searchable text content, and tables have structured columns — each needs a different approach
Text is always more relevant than images
Different scoring strategies take too long to compute
questions.explanation: Text has content that can be searched directly, but images rely on metadata (alt text, tags) for matching, and tables have column names that indicate their structure. Each type needs a strategy that matches its data format.

questions.question: What is the 'visual query boost' and when should it be applied?
choices: A boost applied to all documents when any query is made
A multiplier for image scores when the query contains visual language like 'show,' 'see,' or 'photo'
A penalty applied to text documents to make images rank higher
A boost applied only to table documents
questions.explanation: When a user asks 'show me a sunset photo,' they're clearly looking for an image. The visual query boost (e.g., 1.5x) increases image scores when the query contains visual language, matching user intent.

questions.question: Why should each RAG result include a 'reason' field?
choices: It makes the output more verbose
It helps users understand why a document was ranked highly, enabling trust and debugging
It's required by the RAG protocol
Reasons are only needed for failed searches
questions.explanation: Results without reasons are opaque. If a user sees an unexpected document ranked highly, the reason ('Image metadata match: 3/5' or 'Table column match: 2/4') helps them understand and trust the ranking.
